about.title: Personal Injury Help in Laguna Woods, California
about.longDescription: Laguna Woods is a quiet, close-knit community, but it isn't immune to serious collisions. In the most recent full year on record, the city saw 29 injury collisions and 42 people hurt, including one traffic death. Much of that activity concentrates along El Toro Road and Moulton Parkway, two corridors that carry a lot of the town's day-to-day traffic, with crashes tending to cluster on Saturday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. If you or someone you love was hurt in one of these incidents, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and next steps can feel overwhelming on top of physical recovery. Our team handles personal injury claims in Laguna Woods and throughout Orange County. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover compensation for you. There's no cost and no obligation to find out whether you have a claim worth pursuing. Reaching out early can help preserve evidence and protect your options while California's filing deadlines are still open.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it pays to check early.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering in ordinary injury cases, which can matter a great deal for serious injuries.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless We Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront fee. We only get paid if we recover money on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Laguna Woods?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If a government agency, like a city road department, is potentially involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do injury collisions tend to cluster in Laguna Woods?
items.answer: Public crash records show a higher concentration of collisions along El Toro Road and Moulton Parkway, with Saturday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. seeing more reported crashes than other times. This is simply a pattern in the public data, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your total recovery would just be reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. There is no charge for a free case review. We work on contingency, so you don't pay unless we recover money for you.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. The actual amount depends on the specifics of your injury and case, which we would need to review.
